deep.reconstruction:
The page holds two unrelated layers.

(A) Upright layer, dated 'Göttingen 1850, Mai 30. 31' (a '185' was started and struck). This is a draft of a header or caption for a protocol of magnetic observations with the Gauss–Weber bifilar magnetometer.
- Riemann tries several wordings of one statement and strikes most of them. The surviving sense is: 'The observed value k holds for the stated time according to Pennington's chronometer, whose rate (Gang) and error (Stand) differed only slightly from mean time (M. Z. = mittlere Zeit).'
- A second heading reads 'Constanten des Bifilarmagnetometers, Mai 22'. Under it are the empty slots 'P =', 'Q =', 'log R =', 'log S ='. These are evidently reduction constants to be filled in later. They plausibly serve converting scale readings to relative variations of horizontal intensity, and temperature or torsion corrections. This reading is mine; the page gives no values or formulas.
- A further reworded sentence repeats that the observations were made with a Pennington chronometer whose rate and error differed very little from mean time.
- No computation is carried out. The context is Riemann's 1850 participation in Wilhelm Weber's physical work and mathematical-physical seminar in Göttingen, where magnetometer observations were routine.

(B) Upside-down layer, about 25 dense Kurrent lines with heavy deletions. It cannot be transcribed reliably. Isolated symbols are visible (Q, Z, T, 0.0 and similar), and plausible words include Fläche, Punkt, Werthe.
- Given the neighbouring folios, this is very probably a draft passage of the 1851 doctoral dissertation (Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse). The likely region is around §§16–18, on surfaces spread over the plane, points, and boundary values.
- The paper was evidently reused scrap. No derivation is legible enough to reconstruct.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no mathematics beyond an unfilled list of instrument constants for a bifilar magnetometer, plus an illegible inverted draft of dissertation text. Riemann's 1850 involvement with Weber's magnetic observations and the content of his dissertation are both well known.
transcription_corrections: The word inserted above 'Pennington's' looks like 'Uhr' (or a superscript abbreviation). The phrase reads roughly 'nach Pennington's Uhr, dessen Gang und Stand ... M. Z. ... wenig abwich'. Several struck words between 'Stand' and 'M. Z.' are not 'sehr nahe' with certainty.
The insertion above 'wenig abwich' in line 4 is uncertain ('einem'/'nur'); it is best left as [?].
'Chronom.' before 'Constanten' is doubtful from the image. It may be a separate struck or partial word rather than part of the heading 'Constanten des Bifilarmagnetometers'.
The upside-down block is probably a dissertation draft (cf. §§16–17 on adjacent folios), not physics notes. The isolated symbols should not be read as numerical data.
